$comment: Generated from rb-mcp's tool definitions by `RB_UPDATE_SCHEMA=1 cargo nextest run -p rb-mcp mcp_tools_file`; do not edit by hand.

tools.name: app_info
tools.description: rBrowser's version, commit, build time and platform, the engine versions (CEF/Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, Node), the API versions and the data and log folders - the facts of Settings > About, without the licence texts.

tools.name: back
tools.description: Go back in the history of the targeted views and answer their final URLs. A view without history stays where it is. target: "all" (default), a view id or a breakpoint id.

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: `"all"` (default), a view id, or a breakpoint id.

tools.name: bookmarks_list
tools.description: List the project's bookmarks: for each id, label, group and shortcut if any, relative (true: it stores a path such as /shop/cart?x=1#top and follows the environment; false: an absolute URL, the same everywhere), its path when relative, and url - where it leads in the environment in effect (absent for a path with no environment or start URL to lie under). Also environment (the one in effect), base (the URL paths are put after) and followEnvironment (the setting bookmarks.followEnvironment: new bookmarks of a page under an environment are stored as paths). A read only; acts on no view. Open one with navigate and its url.
tools.withoutCommand: a read: the project's bookmarks, each with relative and the URL it leads to now

tools.name: bookmarks_make_relative
tools.description: Turn every bookmark with an absolute URL that lies under the project's environments into a path, so it follows the environment from then on (https://staging.example.com/shop/cart becomes /shop/cart). Only a URL whose path leads to the same page under every environment that names its host is converted; a foreign host, or environments with different base paths on that host, keep the URL. Edits only bookmarks[] of config.json and config.local.json (both written or neither), reads the config again and tells the person the number in the status bar. Answers converted (how many), ids, and invalid (bookmarks the config check refuses, left as they are) when there are any. Takes no arguments; acts on no view.

tools.name: breakpoint_add
tools.description: Add a breakpoint to the project config: breakpoint as in breakpoints[] (id, width, height, label, device, emulation, ...; request headers are refused). Checked before it is written; the grid follows.

guard.note: Request headers are guarded by workspace trust and refused with code config_key_protected.

ConfigScope.description: Which project file `config_set` and the breakpoint tools write.

tools.name: breakpoint_remove
tools.description: Remove a breakpoint from the project config by id. Refused when the layout still names it (the check says where).
tools.withoutCommand: edits the project config as the settings window does; no command removes a breakpoint

ConfigScope.description: Which project file `config_set` and the breakpoint tools write.

tools.name: breakpoint_update
tools.description: Change a breakpoint of the project config: id, fields to merge (null removes a field; request headers are refused). Checked before it is written.

guard.note: Request headers are guarded by workspace trust and refused with code config_key_protected.

tools.withoutCommand: edits the project config as the settings window does; no command changes a breakpoint

ConfigScope.description: Which project file `config_set` and the breakpoint tools write.

fields.description: The fields to change; objects merge, `null` removes a field.

tools.name: breakpoints_apply
tools.description: Write proposed breakpoints into .rbrowser/config.json: proposalId (default the last), selected ids (default every new one), replace instead of add.

proposalId.description: The proposal of a `breakpoints_detect` call; the last one when absent.

selected.description: The proposed breakpoint ids to write; every new one when empty.

replace.description: Replace the config's breakpoints instead of adding to them.

tools.name: breakpoints_detect
tools.description: Find the breakpoints a site's CSS uses (media queries, container queries) and propose views for them; writes nothing. urls: the pages (default the start URL), mode: all, simplified or edges. The answer carries a proposalId for breakpoints_apply.

urls.description: The pages to read; the project's start URL when empty.

mode.description:
`all` (a view per breakpoint), `simplified` (five groups) or `edges` (a view at every
edge +/- 1 px); the project's mode when absent.

tools.name: bus_send
tools.description: Send a message on the page API's message bus (window.__rbrowser.bus) to the pages of `target` ("all" (default), a view id or a breakpoint id): their bus.on(type) handlers get `payload` with from: null. `type` is 1 to 64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : / -; `payload` any JSON value up to bus.maxPayloadBytes. Answers the views whose page took it (delivered) and the ones that did not (skipped): a page with the bus or the page API off, or without the sync agent.
tools.withoutCommand: puts a message on the page API's bus from outside; no command sends one

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: `"all"` (default), a view id or a breakpoint id.

type.description: The message type: 1 to 64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : / -.

payload.description: Any JSON value, up to `bus.maxPayloadBytes`; `null` when left out.

tools.name: canvas_place
tools.description: Canvas layout: move one view (target: a view id or breakpoint id, default the active view) to x/y on the canvas in DIP, optionally with its zoom (0.1 to 1). The place snaps to the preset's grid and to neighbouring views' edges and is written into the current canvas preset, else into the top-level layout's `layout.modes.canvas`; the answer has the snapped x/y and whether the view is in sight.

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: The view: a view id or a breakpoint id; the active view when absent.

x.description: The view's left edge on the canvas, in canvas DIP (snapped).

y.description: The view's top edge on the canvas, in canvas DIP (snapped; its label sits above).

zoom.description: The view's zoom, 0.1 to 1; unchanged when absent.

tools.name: canvas_zoom
tools.description: Canvas layout: zoom the canvas. level is the active view's page zoom - 1 shows its page at its real size (100 %), 0.5 at half, at most 2 (the largest view stays at 200 % at most) - or "fit" for every view in sight; 100 % when absent. The active view stays in the middle of the area. Answers { level }, the level set. Fails outside the canvas layout.

anyOf.description: The active view's page zoom: 1 for 100 %, up to 2.
`"fit"`: every view in sight.

level.description:
The page zoom of the active view (1 = 100 %, 0.5 = 50 %, at most 2), or `"fit"` for
every view in sight; 100 % when absent.

tools.name: cdp_endpoint
tools.description: The CDP endpoint for Playwright connectOverCDP(url, { headers }) and other CDP clients: url with its Authorization header, urlWithToken for clients without headers, the browser webSocketDebuggerUrl, with target also the page socket of that view, and wsl: the URL from WSL (Windows' own in mirrored mode, a tunnel into the distribution in NAT mode). Only the grid's views are targets. rBrowser owns each view's size: setViewportSize has no effect. Off unless a person switched the proxy on (cdp.enabled, code cdp.disabled) and allowed page JavaScript over MCP (mcp.allowEvaluate, code evaluate_disabled): the endpoint is full control of the page.

guard.note: Off until a person switches on the setting cdp.enabled (code cdp.disabled) and mcp.allowEvaluate (code evaluate_disabled): the endpoint is full control of the page.

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: One view (id or breakpoint id): its page socket is added.

tools.name: checks_cancel
tools.description: Cancel the check run in progress (checks_run, the findings panel's Run checks): jobs not started are skipped, running ones are dropped; the findings of the jobs that finished stay and are the run's answer, with cancelled: true. Answers cancelled: false when no run is in progress. Acts on no view.

tools.name: checks_run
tools.description: Run every enabled check plugin (SEO, accessibility, console, ...) over the views of `target` ("all" (default), a view id or a breakpoint id) and answer the merged findings - deduplicated across views and plugins, each with a stable id - a summary per severity and plugin, and how each plugin x view job ended (jobs: done with its count, failed with its code, skipped with the reason). `plugins` limits the run to those plugin ids, `url` checks that page instead of the views' own. checks_cancel stops a run in progress (cancelled: true). The run is also written to .rbrowser/out/checks/.

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: `"all"` (default), a view id or a breakpoint id.

plugins.description: Only these check plugins (ids); every enabled one when absent.

url.description: The page to check, http(s); each view's own when absent.

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click an element (CSS `selector`) as real input in the views of `target` ("all", a view id or a breakpoint id; the active view when absent): `button` left (default), middle or right, `clickCount` 1 to 3, `modifiers` (Alt, Control, Meta, Shift). Touch views get a tap. Answers per view done, notFound, notVisible or a failure.
tools.withoutCommand: replays a click into the views over CDP; no command clicks an element

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: `"all"`, a view id or a breakpoint id; the active view when absent.

tools.name: config_get
tools.description: Read the effective project config (.rbrowser/config.json merged with config.local.json), secrets masked; key picks one dotted key (breakpoints, layout.gap).
tools.withoutCommand: a read: the effective project config

key.description: A dotted key (`layout.gap`); everything when absent.

tools.name: config_set
tools.description: Change one key of the project config (.rbrowser/config.json, or config.local.json with scope local): key dotted, value (null removes). The result is checked as the settings window checks it. Keys guarded by workspace trust (headers, network, plugins, extensions) are refused with code config_key_protected.

guard.note: Keys guarded by workspace trust (headers, network, plugins, extensions) are refused with code config_key_protected.

ConfigScope.description: Which project file `config_set` and the breakpoint tools write.

value.description: The new value; `null` removes the key.

tools.name: console_logs
tools.description: The console messages of the targeted views since the MCP server started (or the last clear): level, source, text, url, line, time (ms since epoch); newest last. level filters, limit caps per view (default 100), clear empties the buffer. Buffer size: setting mcp.consoleLogLimit.
tools.withoutCommand: a read: the console buffer of the views

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: `"all"` (default), a view id or a breakpoint id.

limit.description: The most entries per view, the newest (default 100).

failedOnly.description: `network_requests`: only failed requests and HTTP errors (status 400 and up).

tools.name: cookies_copy
tools.description: Copy the cookies of a Chromium session into the Firefox and WebKit views of that session, so a login in the grid holds there too (each view loads its page again unless engines.cookies.reload is off). source: a session id or a view id (default: each view's own session); target: "all" (default), a view id or a breakpoint id; domains: only these sites (default: engines.cookies.domainFilter). Answers per view the cookies copied, refused and skipped with their reasons - never a cookie value; without a Firefox or WebKit view it says so in `message`.

anyOf.description: A view id: that view's session.
A session id: `default` or one of the project's `sessions`.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

source.description:
The session to copy from: a session id or a view id (its session). Absent: each Firefox
or WebKit view gets the cookies of its own session.

target.description: `"all"` (every Firefox and WebKit view, the default), a view id or a breakpoint id.

domains.description:
Only the cookies of these sites (host names, a parent domain's cookies included);
absent: the setting `engines.cookies.domainFilter`.

tools.name: devtools_inspect_at
tools.description: Open DevTools for one view (target: a view id or breakpoint id, default the active view; mode as the setting) and select the element at the point x, y - CSS px of the page, from the viewport's top-left corner - in the Elements panel, like the page's context menu entry Inspect element. Always opens DevTools when they are closed or with another view: the setting devtools.openOnInspect holds back only the menu entry and the shortcut. Answers the view, the DevTools mode, the element's backendNodeId and selected (false in a DevTools window, which takes no selection).

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: One view (id or breakpoint id); the active view when absent.

x.description: The point's x, in CSS px of the view's page from its top-left corner.

y.description: The point's y, in CSS px of the view's page from its top-left corner.

tools.name: devtools_open
tools.description: Open DevTools for one view (target: a view id or breakpoint id, default the active view); mode docked-bottom, docked-right or window (default the setting).

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: One view (id or breakpoint id); the active view when absent.

mode.description: `docked-bottom`, `docked-right` or `window`; the setting's mode when absent.

tools.name: diagnostics
tools.description: Write the diagnostics ZIP (logs, crash dumps, versions, the masked config) into the diagnostics folder and answer its path. Nothing is sent anywhere.

out.description: A file name ending in `.zip` inside the diagnostics folder; a fresh name when absent.

tools.name: emulation_set
tools.description: Change the emulation of the targeted views live ("all", a view id or a breakpoint id; default the active view): fields as in a breakpoint's emulation. Answers the views changed and whether a reload is needed.

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: `"all"`, a view id or a breakpoint id; the active view when absent.

fields.description:
The emulation fields to set (a breakpoint's `emulation` in the config: colorScheme,
reducedMotion, userAgent, locale, timezone, network, ...); absent fields stay.

tools.name: engine_restart
tools.description: Restart an external engine's views (engine: "firefox" or "webkit"): every view of that engine, or those of `target` ("all" (default), a view id or a breakpoint id). Each view opens again with its last URL. Fails with a readable message when no view of that engine is open or the engine is not available. Answers the restarted view ids.

ExternalEngine.description:
The engines that run in windows of their own; Chromium runs the grid and restarts only with
rBrowser.

oneOf.description: WebKit through Playwright in the sidecar.

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description: `"all"` (every view of the engine, the default), a view id or a breakpoint id.

tools.name: engines_list
tools.description: List the installed Firefox editions rBrowser can drive: for each its path, kind (release, esr, developer, nightly) and version, in the order rBrowser searches (the registry's App Paths and uninstall entries, then the editions' folders under Program Files and the local app data); the first is what an empty engines.firefox.path starts. Also the configured path and, when it names no file any more, missing: true. A read only; acts on no view and starts nothing.
tools.withoutCommand: a read: the installed Firefox editions; the path is the person's setting

tools.name: env_compare
tools.description: Compare the same pages in two or more environments (local, staging, prod) pixel by pixel. target ("all" or views; the active view's page when absent) picks the breakpoints and the page; optional environments (ids, at least two), paths (/about or a URL under an environment; a foreign host is refused), breakpoints, fullPage, threshold (0 to 1). Each path is captured in every environment and breakpoint in hidden render views (the grid stays usable) and every environment pair is diffed. Answers at once with runId, the folder .rbrowser/out/env-compare/<runId>/ (PNGs, diff images, report.json, report.html) and the shots and diffs; follow it with env_compare_result. One run at a time. hideBanners and freezeAnimations override capture.hideBanners and capture.freezeAnimations (banners hidden, animations frozen before each capture, undone after).

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description:
`"all"`, a view id or a breakpoint id: the views whose breakpoints (and the first one's
page) are compared; the active view's page and the setting envCompare.breakpoints when
absent.

environments.description:
Environment ids (at least two); envCompare.environments, else every environment, when
absent.

paths.description: Paths (`/about`) or URLs under an environment; the target view's page when absent.

breakpoints.description: Breakpoint ids; over the target views' breakpoints.

threshold.description: The colour tolerance, 0 to 1 (over envCompare.threshold and visual.threshold).

hideBanners.description: Hide cookie banners and chat widgets; the setting capture.hideBanners when absent.

freezeAnimations.description: Freeze animations and videos; the setting capture.freezeAnimations when absent.

tools.name: env_compare_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a running environment comparison (runId; the running one when absent). The shots taken stay, report.json and report.html are written for what was compared, and the run's state becomes cancelled. Answers the runId and whether it was still running.

runId.description:
The run (`env_compare` answers it); the latest (for a cancel: the running one) when
absent.

tools.name: env_compare_live
tools.description: Show one view's breakpoint once per environment side by side (target: one view; the active view when absent), each on the page the view shows under its own environment, synced: a click on an internal link moves every view to the same path under its own host, a link to another host is not rewritten. Optional environments (ids), enabled (false returns to the grid before; toggles when absent). Answers whether it shows and each view's environment and URL.

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

target.description:
One view (a view id, or a breakpoint id shown once) whose breakpoint and page are
compared; the active view when absent.

environments.description: Environment ids; envCompare.environments, else every environment, when absent.

enabled.description: true shows the comparison, false leaves it; toggles when absent.

tools.name: env_compare_result
tools.description: The state of an environment comparison (runId; the latest when absent): running or finished, the shots taken and failed, the pairs that differ, the folder and report.html once written, and per path, environment pair and breakpoint the status (same, differs, sizeMismatch, failed, pending), the share of differing pixels in percent and the diff image.

runId.description:
The run (`env_compare` answers it); the latest (for a cancel: the running one) when
absent.

tools.name: environment_set
tools.description: Switch to an environment of the config (its base URL in every view).

id.description: An environment id of the config.

tools.name: errors
tools.description: The uncaught exceptions of the targeted views: text, url, line, column, time; newest last. limit caps per view (default 100), clear empties the buffer. Buffer size: setting mcp.errorLimit.
tools.withoutCommand: a read: the error buffer of the views

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

limit.description: The most entries per view, the newest (default 100).

failedOnly.description: `network_requests`: only failed requests and HTTP errors (status 400 and up).

tools.name: evaluate
tools.description: Run a JavaScript expression in the page of the targeted views (main world) and answer each view's value (by value; promises awaited). Off by default: a person switches it on with the setting mcp.allowEvaluate; while off the answer is an error with code evaluate_disabled and settingsKey. Answers are masked and cut at mcp.maxAnswerBytes. target: "all" (default), a view id or a breakpoint id.

guard.note: Off until a person switches on the setting mcp.allowEvaluate; while off it answers code evaluate_disabled.

tools.withoutCommand: runs page JavaScript over CDP; no command runs a script

TargetArg.description: What a tool's `target` says, as written.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

expression.description: A JavaScript expression, run in the page's main world.

target.description: `"all"` (default), a view id or a breakpoint id.

awaitPromise.description: Wait for a promise the expression returns (default true).

timeoutMs.description: How long it may run, in milliseconds (default 10000, at most 60000).

tools.name: extension_install
tools.description: Install an extension from the Chrome Web Store (id: the extension id or its store page URL). rBrowser downloads it from Google's update server, checks its CRX3 signatures (the developer's key is the id, the Web Store's key the publisher) and then asks the person in its window; only their Install unpacks it, and it loads into every Chromium view at the next start (restartNeeded true). Declined or not answered within ten minutes: code extensions.declined. Off while engines.chromium.extensions.allowWebStore is off (code extensions.web_store_off, settingsKey). No tool grants the confirmation.
tools.actsOn: the Chrome extensions of the instance

guard.note: Off while engines.chromium.extensions.allowWebStore is off (code extensions.web_store_off); on, nothing is unpacked before the person confirms the install in rBrowser's window (declined: code extensions.declined).

tools.withoutCommand: downloads and checks a Web Store extension, then waits for the person's word in the window; the person's own command extensions.install_web_store asks nothing

id.description: The extension id (32 letters a to p) or its Chrome Web Store page URL.

tools.name: extension_list
tools.description: The Chrome extensions of the Chromium views: enabled (engines.chromium.extensions.enabled), each unpacked folder of the person's list and each extension installed from the Chrome Web Store (source webStore) with its name, version, id, whether this start loaded it or why it is refused, restartNeeded when the set changed since the start, webStore (engines.chromium.extensions.allowWebStore), and a trusted project's recommendations (folders inside the project; a Web Store entry with installable true can be installed with extension_install). A read: no tool loads or removes an unpacked folder - that is the person's command in rBrowser (Extensions: load an unpacked extension, Ctrl+Shift+Space X O); a Web Store extension is removed with extension_remove after the person's word.
tools.actsOn: the Chrome extensions of the instance
tools.withoutCommand: a read: the Chrome extensions; adding one is the person's command, never MCP's

tools.name: extension_remove
tools.description: Remove an extension installed from the Chrome Web Store (id: the extension id or its store page URL). rBrowser names it in its window and deletes its folder under the local store (every version, the pointer, staging leftovers) only on the person's Remove; what this start loaded stays loaded until the next start (restartNeeded true then). Not installed from the store: code extensions.not_installed; declined or not answered within ten minutes: code extensions.declined. Off while engines.chromium.extensions.allowWebStore is off (code extensions.web_store_off, settingsKey). Unpacked folders are never removed. No tool grants the confirmation.
tools.actsOn: the Chrome extensions of the instance

guard.note: Off while engines.chromium.extensions.allowWebStore is off (code extensions.web_store_off); on, nothing is deleted before the person confirms the removal in rBrowser's window (declined: code extensions.declined).

id.description: The extension id (32 letters a to p) or its Chrome Web Store page URL.

tools.name: flow_list
tools.description: The project's flows (.rbrowser/flows/*.ts: Playwright scripts with page, view, expect, env and step injected) with their description and views, whether the workspace is trusted (flows run only then; trust is a person's decision in rBrowser), the run going on with each view's status, and the last run's result file.
tools.withoutCommand: a read: the project's flows, the trust state and the runs; no command lists them

tools.name: flow_run
tools.description: Runs a flow in every chosen view at once and answers per view passed, failed, skipped (Firefox and WebKit views, with the reason) or timedOut, with duration, steps, the error with its step and line, and a screenshot file on failure - the same result.json the shell and `rbrowser flow run` show. Refused with flows.untrusted until a person trusts the workspace; one run at a time (flows.busy).

guard.note: A flow is project code: it runs only in a workspace a person trusted, otherwise it answers code flows.untrusted; no tool grants trust.

wait.description:

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

tools.description: Move the mouse onto an element (CSS `selector`) in the views of `target` ("all", a view id or a breakpoint id; the active view when absent), so :hover styles and hover menus open. Answers per view.

anyOf.description: A view id (`views_list`).
`"all"`, a view id as text, or a breakpoint id: every view showing that breakpoint.

tools.name: layout_save_preset
tools.description: Save the layout shown now as a named layout preset and select it: the mode with its fields - the canvas with every view's place (not the camera), the split's ratio and sides, the strip's height, the grid in effect, focus mode's breakpoint. file is local (config.local.json, the default unless the user setting layoutModes.savePresetTo says project) or project (config.json, shared with the team); a preset of that id in that file is replaced. tools.description: Add a view of a new size or of a device preset: pass width and height (dpr optional), or device (a device preset id: its size, pixel ratio, user agent and touch apply). A breakpoint (name, else size-<width>x<height> or an id made from the device id) is written into config.local.json, the config is read again and the view opens - an explicit layout.cells grid gets a column for it. A breakpoint of that id that exists with the same size or device is opened instead; one with another size or device is refused - choose another name. Answers what is open in the end: breakpoint, width, height, added (false when it existed), changed (false when its view was open already) and hidden; for a device breakpoint also device and dpr.
tools.actsOn: the project config and the hidden selection of the views

width.description: Width in CSS px, 1 to 16384; with `height`, unless `device` is given.

device.description:
A device preset's id (`devices_list`) instead of `width` and `height`: the view gets
the preset's size, pixel ratio, user agent and touch.

name.description:
The breakpoint's id (letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`); `size-<width>x<height>` or the
device's id when absent.

dpr.description: A device pixel ratio, above 0 and at most 10; not with `device`.

x.description: Canvas: where the view goes, in canvas DIP (both or neither).

tools.name: view_metrics
tools.description: Read the Web Vitals and resources of the targeted views (target: "all" (default), a view id or a breakpoint id). Per view: vitals lcp, cls, inp, fcp and ttfb, each with value (ms; CLS unitless), rating ("good", "needs-improvement" or "poor" by web.dev's thresholds, overridable in vitals.thresholds) and the element behind it (lcp element, cls sources, inp target as CSS paths); resources cpuPercent (the page's main-thread share), memoryMb (its JS heap), cpuWarn and ramWarn (resources.cpuWarnPercent, resources.ramWarnMb); throttle (visible, hidden or cpuLimited); segment and soft (a soft navigation measures only CLS and INP). A missing value is {na, reason}: pending (not measured yet, e.g. INP before an interaction), unsupported or engine (the engine cannot give it; Firefox and WebKit views have no resources), soft, or off with the settingsKey that switched it off.
tools.withoutCommand: a read: the Web Vitals and resources of the views

tools.name: view_page_zoom
tools.description: Zoom the page inside the targeted views as Chrome's Ctrl+Plus, Ctrl+Minus and Ctrl+0 do (Chromium's page zoom, not the grid's zoom of a cell). A zoomed page lays out at another CSS width than its breakpoint's, so breakpoints apply differently; the view's label strip shows the level. level: a factor (1 = 100 %, 0.25 to 5), "in" or "out" for one of Chromium's steps (25 % to 500 %); 100 % when absent. With the user setting views.pageZoom.sync every view takes the level; Chromium keeps a zoom per site, so views of one session on the same host zoom together. Only Chromium views zoom. target: "all", a view id or a breakpoint id; default the active view. Answers views: [{ view, level, percent }].

tools.description: List the views of the grid in grid order: id (the `target` of every view tool), label, breakpoint (null after a free size), cellBreakpoint, engine, width, height, dpr, scale, url, title, loading, session and cell; desync (null while the view is in sync, else the reason, the event and the selector that failed), syncNavigation (whether the view follows the active view's navigation), detached (the view is in a window of its own, view_pop_out), range (the widths the view stands for among the breakpoints of the config, as its breakpoint bar shows them: from - 0 for the smallest breakpoint - and to, null for the largest), external (a Firefox or WebKit view in a window of its own) with its status, externalWindow (open while that window runs or is starting, closed when the person closed it, it crashed or could not start; engine_restart opens it again) and embedded (true while that window sits in its grid cell, setting engines.external.embed; false while it is a window of its own); frameworks (what the page runs of Vue and React while their Framework DevTools are not off: per framework version, hook - rBrowser's DevTools hook is in the document - and devtools - the framework talks to it; {} when none).

tools.name: views_set_engine
tools.description: Set the engine of the targeted views (target: "all", a view id or a breakpoint id; default the active view) to chromium, firefox or webkit. The engine is written as breakpoints[].engine of each view's breakpoint into file local (config.local.json, the default) or project (config.json, shared with the team), the config is read again and the view follows - Firefox and WebKit in external windows. An engine that cannot run (Firefox not found, WebKit not installed) is refused with the reason. Answers per view { view, breakpoint, engine, file, changed } - changed is false when a config.local.json entry of the breakpoint shadows a project write - or { view, failed } for a view without a breakpoint of the config; target all is one write and one reload.

tools.name: visual_compare
tools.description: Compare views with their baselines in .rbrowser/baselines/<page>/<breakpoint>.png (target "all" (default), a view id or a breakpoint id): each view is captured, diffed pixel by pixel with anti-aliasing tolerance and answered as ok, differs (share of differing pixels, bounding boxes, diff image path), new (no baseline), sizeMismatch or failed, with the metadata fields that make a comparison unreliable (another machine, DPI or engine version). threshold (0 to 1) overrides visual.threshold. The findings also go to the findings panel; regressions counts differs and sizeMismatch. One run at a time. hideBanners and freezeAnimations override capture.hideBanners and capture.freezeAnimations (banners hidden, animations frozen before each capture, undone after).
